# Urbo

Urbo is an open source smart city app platform that retrieves services and information from various
sources and makes them available on a single platform for citizens.

The app accesses data from city-specific backends and bundles the available content into thematic-functional
modules. Cities can configure which modules are active and adapt the branding to their own identity.

The available feature modules are:

- News
- Events
- Citizen services
- Feedback/Support
- Parking
- POIs
- Waste calendar
- Construction sites
- Funfair / Special events
- Citizen participation
- Surveys (LimeSurvey)
- Link lists
- Image spotlight
- NINA emergency alerts
- Here & Now (smart recommendations)
- Push notifications
- User account management (profile, account deletion)

Urbo is developed and maintained by [SWCode](https://swcode.io).

## Project status

Urbo is **actively developed** and in production. It runs as the citizen app of several German
cities, and development continues on `main` with releases cut from `app-v*` tags — at the time of
writing, several times per working day (278 `app-v2.0.x` releases since 2026-06-22, an average of
roughly 4-5 per working day).

- **Releases:** every release is an `app-v*` tag, listed at
  [gitlab.opencode.de/urbo-community/urbo/-/tags](https://gitlab.opencode.de/urbo-community/urbo/-/tags).
- **Versioning:** how the version numbers are formed and what a bump means is described in
  [docs/versioning.md](./docs/versioning.md).
- **Where it is going:** the feature modules listed above are the delivered scope. Work in
  progress and planned changes are tracked as issues and design documents under
  [docs/plans/](./docs/plans/).
- **Contributing:** see [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). Security reports go through
  [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md), not the issue tracker.

## Development

One command brings up everything for the worktree you are in — backend, CMS, citizen app and
urboards — with dependencies installed, the database seeded, and no port conflicts with any other
worktree:

```bash
just up
```

The first run asks for an instance identifier (the worktree directory name is offered as the
default) and remembers it in `.urbo-instance`. Every URL is derived from that identifier, so two
worktrees — two branches, two PRs you're reviewing side by side — can run at the same time without
touching each other's database, search index or file storage:

```
http://app.<instance>.localhost
http://cms.<instance>.localhost
http://boards.<instance>.localhost
http://api.<instance>.localhost
```

`.localhost` is the reserved TLD that every browser and OS resolves straight to `127.0.0.1` without
a DNS lookup — no `/etc/hosts` editing, no internet access needed. It also gets the frontends a
*secure context* (so `crypto.subtle` exists and Keycloak's login works): browsers grant that only to
`localhost` itself or a name ending in `.localhost`, never to a name that merely resolves to
loopback. `just urls` prints the full list (Keycloak, MeiliSearch, LocalStack, imgproxy, Mailpit, ...)
whenever you need to find them again, `just open cms` opens one straight in the browser, and
`just ls` shows every instance currently running on the machine, across all worktrees.

Start instances one at a time. Two `just up` runs beginning at the same moment are not guarded
against each other — there is no lockfile around the shared proxy setup — so a concurrent start can
race. This was judged not worth a lockfile for a local dev tool; just avoid starting two at once.

A `GITHUB_TOKEN` (classic PAT with `read:packages`) is required to build the backend image; `just up`
checks for it up front and fails at that preflight step, with the fix, rather than partway through a
multi-minute build — see [`backend/README.md`](./backend/README.md) for how to set it up.

### When something doesn't come up

Run `just doctor` on its own: it repeats the same preflight checks (Docker, Node, pnpm, `just`
itself, the Docker daemon, the shared proxy's port, `GITHUB_TOKEN`) and prints a fix for anything
that fails, without touching any container.

Beyond that:

- `just status` shows this instance's containers; `just logs` follows all of them, or pass a
  service name (e.g. `just logs spring-app`) to follow just one.
- `just sh <service>` opens a shell inside a running container.
- `just down` stops this instance's containers but keeps its data; `just reset` also deletes its
  volumes (database, search index, file storage) for a clean slate; `just fresh` wipes this
  instance's data and brings it straight back up, freshly seeded, in one step.
- `just reset-auth` re-imports this instance's Keycloak realm, keeping every bit of seeded content.
  Keycloak's `start-dev --import-realm` never overwrites a realm that already exists, so editing the
  realm template (a new client, a changed `URBO_PROXY_PORT`, ...) against an already-seeded instance
  is otherwise a silent no-op — `just up` itself now catches this and tells you to run `reset-auth`,
  but reach for it directly whenever login stops working with `Invalid parameter: redirect_uri`.
- `just prune` removes leftover Docker networks/volumes from instances you deleted without running
  `just reset` first.

### Other recipes

| Recipe | What it's for |
|--------|----------------|
| `just serve` | Start only the three dev servers, against an instance that's already up (what `just up --detach` skips). |
| `just backend-local` | Run the Spring Boot backend on the host with Gradle, wired to this instance's infrastructure — for a fast edit/restart loop instead of rebuilding the container image. Stop the containerised backend first. |
| `just native ios` / `just native android` | Build the citizen app and open it in Xcode / Android Studio, pointed at this instance. Android reaches the proxy through the host's LAN address instead of `*.localhost`, since the emulator's own loopback isn't the host's — `just native android` sets that up for you. **Login does not work on Android:** `KC_HOSTNAME` is pinned to the `<instance>.localhost` URL, which Keycloak then advertises as the issuer/redirect host — an address the emulator cannot resolve. API and search calls work; the login flow does not. This has not been verified against a real emulator; treat it as a known gap, not a tested workaround. |
| `just test-scripts` | Run the unit tests for the orchestration scripts themselves (`scripts/urbo/*.mjs`). |

`just up` also accepts `--fresh` (wipe and reseed), `--detach` (skip starting dev servers),
`--no-seed`, `--apps=<names>` (only start some of the three dev servers) and `--with-limesurvey`
(LimeSurvey is opt-in, not part of the default stack). Run `just` (or `just --list`) for the full,
current recipe list — this table is a summary, not the source of truth.

# Urbo CMS Backend

> **Start here:** `just up` from the repository root brings the whole stack up for the worktree
> you are in — this backend included, in a container, with the database seeded. You only need the
> manual steps below when you are working *on* the backend and want a Gradle restart loop, which
> is what `just backend-local` sets up for you. See
> [`scripts/urbo/services.mjs`](../scripts/urbo/services.mjs)'s header comment for how instances
> are isolated — `docs/plans/one-click-run.md` is the original design proposal and predates some
> details of what shipped.
>
> Ports and hostnames in the sections below are the pre-instance defaults. Under `just up` every
> URL carries the instance label — `http://api.<instance>.localhost` — and only Postgres is
> published on the host, on a port `just up` prints.

Welcome to the Urbo CMS Backend! This guide will help you get started with setting up and running the application.

## Requirements

Before you begin, please ensure you have the following installed:

* [Docker](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop)
* [JDK 25](https://jdk.java.net/25/) (required only if you are not using Docker to run the Spring application.)

## Setting Up

Prerequisites: You need a personal access token to Github, either as environment variable `GITHUB_TOKEN` or as gradle
property `swcodeGprKey`. The access token is required to build the project, because it needs to pull packages from
Github.

1. Get a personal access token key on [your Github settings](https://github.com/settings/tokens).
2. Enter your secret token in as `GITHUB_TOKEN` environment variable.
   Alternatively, place your `swcodeGprKey=ghp_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx`
   in your `%USERPROFILE%\.gradle\gradle.properties` along with your username,
   but this does not work with the docker workflow.
3. Remember to restart your terminals and all containers.

All local services are exposed via an nginx reverse proxy using `*.localhost` subdomains — under
`just up`, one per instance. No `/etc/hosts` changes are needed — `.localhost` is the reserved TLD
that every OS resolves straight to `127.0.0.1` with no DNS lookup at all, and — unlike a name that
merely resolves to loopback — it also gets the frontends a secure context, which Keycloak's login
flow needs (see `scripts/urbo/services.mjs`'s `publicHostname`).

| Service | URL |
|---------|-----|
| Backend API | http://api.\<instance>.localhost |
| Keycloak | http://keycloak.\<instance>.localhost |
| MeiliSearch | http://meilisearch.\<instance>.localhost |
| Mailpit | http://mailpit.\<instance>.localhost |
| Sendinblue Mock | http://sendinblue.\<instance>.localhost |
| LocalStack (S3) | http://localstack.\<instance>.localhost |
| imgproxy | http://imgproxy.\<instance>.localhost |
| LimeSurvey | http://limesurvey.\<instance>.localhost (opt-in, see [LimeSurvey](#limesurvey)) |
| PostgreSQL | localhost, on the port `just up` prints each run — `just status` shows it again (Postgres is the only service published on the host; everything else is reached through the proxy, above) |

`just urls` prints the rest of this list already filled in for your instance.

We have two workflows to launch the backend:

- Test workflow: Uses docker so you don't have to install JDKs to build the backend once.
- Dev workflow: Uses your local Java setup with your installed versions, built for hot reloading.

### Tester workflow

The former `spring/docker-compose.spring.yml` overlay is gone: the backend container (`spring-app`,
built from the multi-stage `Dockerfile` — no local JDK required) is now part of the main Compose
file and is started by `just up` from the repository root, image build included. The one-shot
`sample-data-loader` container it also starts waits for the backend `/health` endpoint and then
seeds demo data in three phases (push-integration content, curated categories, admin resources) —
see [Docker Sample Data](#docker-sample-data) for the full layout.

To disable sample imports for a run, `--no-seed`:

```bash
just up --no-seed
```

To rerun the sample data import after changing files in `docker/sample-data/`, from the repository
root, against an already-`up` instance:

```bash
